configuration.summary:
I see skills not just as items on a list, but as abilities developed through curiosity, practice, experience, and continuous learning. Some have grown through building projects, others through academic pursuits, professional responsibilities, or personal exploration.

This page brings together the technologies, tools, and areas of knowledge I've worked with, along with what each of them means to me. Where possible, I've connected a skill to the projects or milestones that helped me develop it. Others stand on their own, representing knowledge and abilities worth sharing in their own right.

More than a measure of proficiency, this is a reflection of what I've explored, what I've learned, and how I've grown along the way.

skills.title: C#
skills.description: C# became one of my core programming languages through years of hands-on software development. Starting with programming fundamentals, I gradually explored its deeper capabilities, from object-oriented design and language features to building complex applications. Today, it remains central to my approach to solving engineering problems and developing reliable software.

skills.title: .NET
skills.description: Working with the .NET ecosystem has shaped much of my backend engineering experience. I've used it to develop APIs, manage data persistence, implement application architectures, and build scalable backend systems. My experience spans technologies such as ASP.NET Core and Entity Framework Core, with an emphasis on maintainability and sound engineering practices.

skills.title: Python
skills.description: Entirely self-taught, my experience with Python grew out of curiosity and a desire to explore beyond my primary development stack. Its versatility has allowed me to experiment with different programming concepts, automate repetitive tasks, and approach problems from new perspectives. I particularly enjoy its simplicity and flexibility when turning ideas into working solutions.

skills.title: JavaScript
skills.description: I started exploring JavaScript independently out of an interest in making the web more interactive, even before encountering it in my BCA coursework. What began as curiosity evolved into a key part of my professional development toolkit. I actively use it alongside TypeScript, React, and Next.js to build modern frontend experiences and full-stack applications.

skills.title: CSS
skills.description: CSS introduced me to the visual and experiential aspects of building for the web. Beyond basic styling, I've explored responsive design, layout systems, animations, and modern UI techniques to create interfaces that work seamlessly across devices. It remains an essential tool in translating design ideas into polished, usable web experiences.
